fact: Ctrl Alt announced that Dubai Land Department's tokenized real-estate project went live using XRPL for on-chain title-deed tokenization.
interpretation: This is production-oriented RWA evidence rather than a purely conceptual XRPL use case, although initial scale was limited.

fact: Ctrl Alt reported Phase Two of the Dubai project with ten tokenized properties worth more than $5M and controlled secondary-market trading; on-chain transactions continued on XRPL.
interpretation: Progression from issuance into secondary-market functionality strengthens the claim that the project moved beyond a one-off announcement.

fact: The Dubai Land Department project advanced to a regulated secondary-market pilot on XRPL with title-deed ownership records synchronized to the official registry.
interpretation: Government-linked production use supports institutional adoption of XRPL, though economic scale remains small relative to global capital markets.

fact: Dubai Land Department states that investor transactions in the pilot are carried out exclusively in UAE dirhams with no use of cryptocurrencies during the pilot phase.
interpretation: This is direct evidence that an XRPL tokenization success can occur without users buying or paying in XRP, highlighting the value-capture bottleneck.

fact: Ctrl Alt reported secondary-market transactions on XRPL but did not state that participants must hold or route value through XRP.
interpretation: The project supports XRPL utility but does not yet establish material XRP-specific inventory demand.

fact: Official XRPL documentation states that token-to-token DEX execution can use XRP as an intermediary through auto-bridging when the XRP-mediated route is cheaper, and payment pathfinding can produce routes with the same effect.
interpretation: This confirms a native economic mechanism for XRP bridge utility, but does not establish current bridge volume, institutional use, or persistent XRP inventory demand.

fact: Ripple's current Ripple Payments page states that cross-border settlement can occur in fiat or stablecoins and that the settlement layer is decoupled from any single issuer's token, with additional stablecoins added as market demand develops.
interpretation: Ripple Payments can grow without structurally requiring XRP, so aggregate Ripple Payments volume is not valid evidence of XRP-specific value capture unless XRP routing or inventory is separately demonstrated.

fact: Ripple's current Payments ODL documentation states that On-Demand Liquidity can use XRP as the bridge currency to exchange one fiat currency for another.
interpretation: An XRP-specific payments mechanism remains documented in Ripple's stack, but absent current route-level volume or inventory data this is weak evidence for material present-day value capture.

fact: SEC-filed schedules of investment for the Bitwise XRP ETF, Canary XRP ETF, Franklin XRP ETF, and Grayscale XRP Trust ETF show aggregate XRP holdings rising from approximately 547.5M XRP at 2025-12-31 to 798.5M XRP at 2026-06-30, an increase of about 251.1M XRP (+45.9%).
interpretation: This is direct evidence of XRP-specific inventory held by regulated spot investment products. It supports the institutional-inventory mechanism, but does not prove bridge utility or that Ripple/XRPL/RLUSD adoption caused the inflows; Grayscale holdings fell materially over the same window, so accumulation was not uniform.
